pr_title: wayland: update remaining legacy VOCTRL usage to options
pr_body:
The remaining legacy VOCTRLs are for the fullscreen and border
properties. For fullscreen this largely just replacing the private
state field with the vo option but there are small semantic
differences that we need to be careful of.

For the border setting, it's trivial as we don't have external
mechanisms for changing the state, but I also can't test it as
I'm not using a compositor that supports it.
pr_comments: As a side note, it does fix #7210.
Updated to, I think, correctly handle starting in the fullscreen state.
There's still a very small regression with cursor behavior, but that's alright. I'll fix that myself. Fixing #7210 is more important. LGTM now so I'll merge it.

issue_context.title: Infinite loop of setting/unsetting fullscreen in wayland
issue_context.body:
### mpv version and platform
mpv git master and sway (1.2-ba8586e2)

### Reproduction steps
Play any video and use sway's keybindings for making a client fullscreen (default: `super+f`). Using mpv's fullscreen keybind (`f`) works normally.

### Expected behavior
mpv goes fullscreen

### Actual behavior
mpv rapidly goes in and out of fullscreen without stopping. Pressing `super+f` again makes it stop. Curiously, pressing `f` (or whatever mpv's fullscreen keybinding is for you) doesn't stop the going in/out of fullscreen behavior but instead just makes it go slower.

### Log file
https://0x0.st/zlHC.txt

This is probably a wayland only thing (at least i3 didn't have this problem). No idea if a similar thing happens in other compositors that have their own fullscreen commands. Something to do with the window state stuff probably caused this and/or exposed a flaw in the wayland code.
comments: Bisected to 78bb158. I probably can fix this along with the VOCTRL and window state stuff in wayland common.

review_comments: I don't think replacing `wl->fullscreen` with `wl->vo_opts->fullscreen` is correct (here or in the other places). Assuming I understand `vo_opts` correctly, it's just merely a replacement for accessing `vo->opts` directly. `wl->fullscreen` is meant to tell you what the state of the window actually is not its option.
I think we still need this one. `handle_toplevel_config` will check the surfaces for you, but it needs to be stored in the wayland struct somehow.
